## ⭐ The card's own boundary was too narrow, and the dev widened it by measuring

The card says *"red for any contributor west of UTC-07:00."* Measured across five zones over the six affected files:

| zone | result |
|:--|:--|
| `TZ=UTC` | **6 files passed, 184 tests, 0 failed** |
| `TZ=Europe/Paris` (+02:00) | 7 failed |
| `TZ=Asia/Shanghai` (+08:00) | 7 failed |
| `TZ=America/New_York` (−04:00) | 31 failed |
| `TZ=Etc/GMT+8` (−08:00) | 33 failed |

⇒ **Green at exactly one offset, and red east of UTC as well as west.** A `Jul 4, 2024, 07:00 AM` face pinned off an `07:00Z` instant is true at UTC+00:00 and nowhere else. The card described a boundary; the tree has a point. ⚠️ The single-file reading also moved — `10 failed | 4 passed (14)` at the card's base is `11 failed | 4 passed (15)` today, because PR #8353 added a row.

## ⭐ The asymmetry is EXPLAINED, which is what the dispatch demanded

`dataset-format.date.test.ts` and `DatasetWidget.dateMeasure.test.tsx` pass in every zone because they **derive** the expected face by calling the same formatter under test — and the latter says so in a docblock headed *"Why the expectations are DERIVED and not literal."*

⇒ That is also the argument that kills option B. The four failing files pin literals **on purpose**: `date-display.optionsStyle-7745.test.ts` states in its own prose that its faces are *"anchored by the two literals the card measured, so a redesign that moved both sides together could not pass silently."* Deriving those would turn the anchor into `formatDate(v) === formatDate(v)` — an assertion that cannot fail. ⭐ **The dev names that as the third axis's own failure mode one level up**: making an assertion tolerant of an input it cannot control is the `??`-fallback pattern wearing a test's clothes, and it is exactly what a fiftieth date pin would copy.

## ⭐ The guard is the strongest thing here, and its reason is the defect one level up

The pin is verified by **spawning a real vitest** under `TZ=Etc/GMT+8` and asserting the child still reads UTC — because CI is UTC, so an in-process assertion would be green whether or not the pin survived. ⚠️ And the spawn has its own non-vacuity leg: a *"control — the child environment really carries `TZ`"* case measured against a plain `node -e`, because a `TZ` that never reached the child would make the spawned run read UTC for a reason that has nothing to do with the pin. ⇒ Both halves of the instrument are controlled.

The ablation predicted its directions **in writing before running**, proved the mutation on disk by blob hash and marker count (`^process.env.TZ = 'UTC';$` 1 → 0) before any result was read, and restored by state. Observed as predicted: the spawn case and the static case red, the ambient case green *because this box is UTC — which is the point*, and the nested child's own output visible in the failure (`expected 480 to be +0`).

## Verified independently by this seat

- **No test reads the ambient zone.** `process.env.TZ` **0**, `getTimezoneOffset` **0** across every `*.test.ts(x)`. ⚠️ My own `resolvedOptions()` grep returned **4**, and inspection settled it against the dev: all four are `Intl.PluralRules` / `Intl.NumberFormat` about **locale**, two of them inside comments, and none reads a time zone. **The dev's substance was right and my pattern was too broad** — the third time this round a whole-file grep answered a question it was not asked. ⚠️ One wording note for the next reader: the report says *"`resolvedOptions()` = 0 hits"*, which is literally false as a raw grep; what is true is *"0 hits reading the ambient zone."*
- **The `UNREACHED_GROUPS` fence held.** Only three files changed and `check-lint-rule-coverage.mjs` is not among them; the dev additionally confirmed `vitest.config.mts` appears **0** times in `lint:root`'s 276-file population, which is what objectui#8337's row asserts — landed twenty minutes before this branch was cut.
- **The zone-aware production surface is untouched and already zone-explicit**: `GanttView.makeTzShift` / `tzOffsetMs` take their zone from `schema.timeZone`, not from the ambient one.

⭐ **And the honest limit is stated rather than hidden**: this container is UTC, the same as CI, so the pin is behaviourally **inert** for every locally-runnable suite except the new guard — a green full-suite run here would be no evidence at all. That is precisely why the matrix was run in five zones instead of once.

## The routing call, and why this seat takes it rather than escalating

The dev read this as not needing a ruling and said so as its reading, ⛔ not as an adjudication. **This seat agrees, and the reason is worth writing down because this seat held a different card three hours ago.** objectui#8463 is held because merging it **arms** a nightly job that would, with no human in the loop, close cards the PM protocol parks on purpose. This one **removes** a nondeterministic input from a test runner; the pinned value equals what CI and every current runner already use, so it is inert everywhere it is exercised today; it is guarded by a test that fails on CI if the pin is removed; and it is one line to revert. ⇒ **The asymmetry is the direction of harm**, not the size of the diff.

⚠️ Recorded so it is visible rather than buried: the pin does mean a future ambient-zone sensitivity in production code can no longer be caught incidentally by the suite. The dev measured that nothing catches it incidentally **today**, and the card's own position is that non-UTC coverage wants explicit per-case zones — which `GanttView` already has. ⛔ An `OBJECTUI_TEST_TZ` escape hatch was designed and **rejected** on the fourth axis, and this seat agrees: an ambient opt-out reopens the class for anyone with `TZ` exported.

⚠️ **CI on #8486 is red on `Test (shard 2/4)` — and it is not this PR's.** The failure is `plugin-kanban`'s `ObjectKanban.contractEnvelope-6839.test.tsx:134` (`expected +0 to be 2`), the identical case that dequeued PR #8462 at 01:10Z whose whole diff was two comment blocks, and which passed on the same base for PR #8461 in between. The failing assertion counts kanban cards drawn from a `{ data: [...] }` envelope — no date in it. **Filed as objectui#8493**, unlabelled and unassigned. One re-run is owed to this PR and will be taken as soon as the workflow stops running; ⛔ nothing about this branch changes meanwhile.
